answer: When an AI‑agent earns a reward, the protocol locks the payout in a delta‑scaled vesting contract that releases copper‑backed credits only after the agent has contributed computational work for a canyon‑wide observation window. Each new identity must post a stake that is burned each epoch, so the attacker pays immediate copper costs proportional to the number of Sybil accounts. Because vesting is rate‑limited, a farm of fake agents can earn at most a trickle of credits while its upfront burn grows linearly with the identity count, making large‑scale attacks economically infeasible.
